description: §1.7, Practice 1.17 solution, last sentence: "a normal quantity strays beyond two standard deviations about one time in twenty-two, and beyond three about one time in $740$." The sentence is about the two-sided quantity P(|X| >= k*sigma) just computed (0.045500 and 0.002700, keys normal_P_abs_gt_2sigma / normal_P_abs_gt_3sigma). 1/0.0455 = 22.0 (correct), but 1/0.0027 = 370.4, not 740. The 740 figure is 1/0.00135 = 1/(1-Phi(3)), i.e. the ONE-sided tail — so the two halves of the sentence use different conventions. Correct text: "...and beyond three about one time in 370" (or state both as one-sided: one in 44 and one in 741).

§0.3 reading guide, §4 bullet ("§4 — Derived distributions and convolution (L11, rec11 P3, B&T §4.1–4.2)") lists only derived distributions, the monotonic shortcut, the linear case, convolution and the sum of two normals. Neither the §4 bullet nor the "Route" line in the §0 summary box mentions covariance/correlation at all, so the note's own map omits a major topic. Add covariance/correlation (L11 slides 7–8, B&T §4.2) to the §4 bullet and to the Route line.

§0.2, Table 0.1: the row "Conditioning on an event $A$" ($p_{X\mid A}$ / $f_{X\mid A}$) has "§2" in the Where column. §2 never treats $f_{X\mid A}$ — grepping g3_s2.html for f_{X|A} returns nothing, and §2.1–§2.9 cover only joint/marginal/conditional-on-a-random-variable, independence, expectation and the three rec09 problems. The only place a density is conditioned on a positive-probability event is §1 (Example 1.4 Step 4: $f_Z(z)=f_{T\mid\{T<5\}}(z)=f_T(z)/\mathbf{P}(T<5)$, cited to B&T §3.5 p. 165). §0.3 reading guide, §2 bullet reads "(L09, rec09, B&T §3.4–3.5)", assigning all of rec09 to §2. The linear-transformation derivation is done from scratch three times and Z=Y/X twice, with zero cross-referencing. f_Y(y)=(1/|a|)f_X((y−b)/a) is derived in full in §1.7 Example 1.9, again in §3.6 Example 3.10 Part 1 (both cases a>0, a<0), and again in §4.1 'The linear case, derived completely'. §1.7 Example 1.9's proof that Y=aX+b is normal silently assumes a>0 but boxes a general conclusion. The chain is F_Y(y)=P(X≤(y−b)/a)=F_X((y−b)/a) justified by 'dividing by the positive a preserves the inequality' (g3_s1.html line ~620), and the result is stated as f_Y(y)=1/(aσ√(2π))·exp{−(y−(aμ+b))²/(2a²σ²)} — with a bare 'a', not |a|, so the density is negative when a<0. The case a<0 is never mentioned here even though the slide's 'Fact' Y~N(aμ+b, a²σ²) is asserted for all a≠0. Fix: state the hypothesis a>0 explicitly, write the prefactor as 1/(|a|σ√(2π)), and forward-reference §3.6 Example 3.10 / §4.1 where the a<0 case is handled.

§3.6 violates the per-topic quality contract on three counts. It is a substantive h3 (three full worked examples, ~30 lines) but has (a) no practice questions at all — the contract requires 1–3 in .ex boxes with <details class="sol"> at the end of every h3 topic; (b) no <div class="warn"> gotcha — the 'Gotcha built in:' text about E[R]=∞ is inline bold prose inside Example 3.8's .ex box, so it will not render as a gotcha box and is invisible to a reader skimming for warnings; (c) no <div class="note"> interpretation box. Fix: promote the E[R]=∞ remark to a real warn div and add two practice items (e.g. 'V uniform on [40,80], 300-mile trip — find f_T and E[T]'; 'X~U[0,2], find the density of Y=1/X and note where the mean fails to exist').

§5.1's master table cites B&T section numbers in a 'Source' column with no 'B&T' prefix, so they read as internal cross-references and collide with this note's own §3.1–§3.6 and §4.1–§4.2. Compounding it, this table — the note's stated 'whole of G3 on one page' — has no column pointing to where in THIS note each row is treated, unlike §0's Table 0.1 which has a 'Where' column. §4.6 'Continuous convolution and the sum of two uniforms' has two <div class="note"> interpretation boxes but no <div class="warn"> gotcha, despite covering the single highest-error-rate operation in the section — getting the limits of ∫f_X(x)f_Y(w−x)dx right when both supports are bounded. The relevant warning exists only as '§5.4 Gotcha 4 — convolution limits', in a different fragment ~400 lines later, and §4.6 does not point to it. Fix: add a warn box at §4.6 stating that the integral runs over {x: f_X(x)>0} ∩ {x: f_Y(w−x)>0} and that this intersection changes with w (which is exactly why the uniform sum is piecewise), or at minimum cross-reference §5.4 Gotcha 4.

§4.8 'Covariance and correlation' is the only h3 in §4 with no <div class="note"> interpretation box (it has defn, thm×4, ex×2, warn, figcap). Four h3 subsections open cold with no motivating prose: §2.6, §2.7, §2.8 (g3_s2.html lines 495, 558, 617) and §4.4 (g3_s4.html line 362) each place a <div class="ex"> immediately after the heading. Practice 4.9 (two fair dice, §4.5) prints a wrong number that contradicts its own algebra: "$p_W(7)=6\cdot\frac{1}{36}=\frac{6}{36}=\frac16\approx0.138889$". $1/6=0.166667$; $0.138889=5/36$ is the probability of a sum of 8. Root cause is in the compute, not just the prose: computes/g3_s4.py line 371 reads `show("p49_p7", float(dice[6]), "= 6/36")` on `dice = np.convolve([1/6]*6,[1/6]*6)`, whose support is 2..12 so index for w=7 is 5, not 6. computes/g3_s4.json therefore carries the self-contradicting pair `p49_p7 = 0.1388888888888889` and `p49_p7_frac = "1/6"`. Fix: `dice[5]`, rerun, and set the HTML value to 0.166667.

§5.1, paragraph after the correspondence table: "...and the covariance/correlation pair $\operatorname{cov}(X,Y)=...$, $\rho=...$ (L11 slides 7–8). Every one of them was proved in G2 §5.3 and is imported here unchanged." This is false. Practice 4.12 spot value: $f_W(1.5)=e^{-1.5}(e-1)=0.3834004996$, which is $0.383400$ to six places; the note prints $0.383401$. computes/g3_s4.json has `uexp_at_1.5 = 0.3834004995642035`, so this is a transcription/rounding slip in the HTML, not in the compute.

Practice 4.4 calls $f_Y(y)=e^{y-e^{y}}$ "the standard Gumbel density". The standard (maximum) Gumbel density is $e^{-y-e^{-y}}$, with mean $+\gamma=+0.577216$; the density derived here is its reflection (the Gumbel distribution for minima), consistent with the note's own computed mean $-0.577216$ (`p44_mean`). Either rename it ("reflected/minimum Gumbel") or note that $-Y$ is standard Gumbel.

Example 3.2, Step 6: "$y = 2$ (a bulb that lasted 2 time units, i.e. longer than the prior mean lifetime $\approx 1/1.25 = 0.8$)". $1/\mathbb{E}[\Lambda]$ is not the prior mean lifetime; $\mathbb{E}[Y]=\mathbb{E}[1/\Lambda]=\int_1^{3/2} 2/\lambda\,d\lambda = 2\ln(3/2)=0.810930$. This is exactly the $\mathbb{E}[g(X)]\ne g(\mathbb{E}[X])$ trap the note flags in §3.6 (Joan) and §4.3 (Gotcha), so it should not be committed in passing here — relabel as "the reciprocal of the prior mean rate" or quote 0.810930.

Practice 3.8: "$\lambda = 3.912$ means noise standard deviation $\sqrt2/\lambda = 0.361504$, roughly a third of the signal separation ($X$ moves by 2 between the two hypotheses, i.e. $\pm1$ about the origin)". 0.3615 is a third of 1 (the half-separation), not of the separation 2 — as a fraction of the stated separation it is about 18%. Say "roughly a third of the distance from the origin to either signal value".

§5 intro claims "one new operation appeared that has no discrete counterpart worth the name, the derived distribution", but the §5.1 correspondence table two paragraphs later gives the discrete counterpart explicitly ($p_Y(y)=\sum_{x:g(x)=y}p_X(x)$, L10 slide 5), §5.3 step 2 of the Recipe repeats it, and §4.5 develops discrete convolution in full. Rephrase (the genuinely new thing is the CDF/Jacobian machinery, not the concept).

§5.2, uniform variance derivation: $\frac{1}{b-a}\big[\frac{u^3}{3}\big]_{-c}^{c}=\frac{1}{b-a}\cdot\frac{c^3-(-c^3)}{3}$. The lower-limit substitution should be $(-c)^3$, not $-c^3$; the numeric value is unaffected but the displayed step is not the substitution it claims to be.

§5.1 Interpretation box: "...why the conditional density $f_{X|Y}(x|y)$ can be defined at all …: both numerator and denominator of $\mathbf{P}(x\le X\le x+\delta\mid y\le Y\le y+\varepsilon)$ carry a factor $\varepsilon$ that cancels before the limit is taken." As written the quantity whose limit is taken is a probability, not a density — the division by $\delta$ is missing. Gotcha 2 in §5.4 states it correctly ("the limit of $\mathbf{P}(\cdot\mid\cdot)/\delta$"); make the two consistent.
The srcref cites "B&T §4.1 (… Examples 4.8, 4.10, Figs 4.2–4.10 …)", but Example 4.10 is never used anywhere in §4 (only Example 4.8 is cited, in §4.3). Drop it or use it.

Table in §5.1 ("The whole of G3 on one page"), CDF row, is mis-columned and shows a stray pipe glyph: the Discrete (G2) cell reads "—" while the Continuous (G3) cell reads "= \sum_{k\le x} p_X(k)  |  = \int_{-\infty}^x f_X(t)dt, and f_X = dF_X/dx" (s5_p01.png, row 5; source g3_s5.html line 39).
